answer: Because the nectar count is verified against the quill text itself, the ember audit records each rejection and the operator cannot amortise one paragraph. Filling 126 aliases thus means producing 126 separate sets of claims, which is authoring work rather than a lookup. An answer claiming a deep mechanism must supply at least 5 distinct supporting claims, and the count is checked before grading so shallow text cannot pass by padding. That is 9 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
